observation_summary: A unit test for the regularized Gamma function failed due to a small numeric mismatch (expected 0.632120558828558 but was 0.6321205587649603). The post-fix diff changes a single numeric constant DEFAULT_EPSILON from 10e-9 to 10e-15 in org.apache.commons.math.special.Gamma.
reasoning_summary: The fix consists solely of changing the value of a constant (DEFAULT_EPSILON). This is an incorrect initialization/assignment of a numeric tolerance used by the Gamma routines; correcting that constant addresses the precision problem. The change is not adding guards, not altering algorithmic logic, nor changing interfaces or concurrency, so Assignment/Initialization is the best fit.
evidence_used: fix_diff_oracle unified_diff: changed 'private static final double DEFAULT_EPSILON = 10e-9;' to 'private static final double DEFAULT_EPSILON = 10e-15;' in org.apache.commons.math.special.Gamma
bug_report_description: notes default epsilon set to 10e-9 and recommends higher precision (1.0e-15); mentions consistency with other functions using 1.0e-15
GammaTest: tests invoke TestUtils.assertEquals(..., 10e-15) indicating the tests expect higher precision
evidence_gaps: Patch context does not show all places where DEFAULT_EPSILON is used (but changing the constant is still direct evidence of an incorrect initialization)
The exact numeric intent (use of '10e-15' vs canonical '1e-14' or '1e-15') is not explained, though the test and bug report indicate higher precision was intended

alternative_types.why_not_primary: No missing or incorrect conditional/guard was added; the fix changes a numeric constant, not validation logic or bounds checks.
The algorithmic logic was not rewritten; only the tolerance constant was changed, which is an initialization issue rather than a procedural computation error.
No method signatures, parameter contracts, or inter-component message formats were changed.
No concurrency, ordering, or synchronization changes are present in the diff.
The fix does not adjust associations among data structures or procedures; it only corrects a constant value.
The capability exists (Gamma functions implemented); the bug was incorrect numeric tolerance, not a missing or new design-level capability.
